reuse.why: The API and forecast reuse getScheduledAmount, and approximate amounts reuse getApproxNumberThreshold, but budget templates retain their own amount dispatch.

duplication.why: Budget templates duplicate the shared helper's selection between ranged, approximate, and single amounts.

placement.why: The arithmetic belongs in shared/schedules, but the budget layer still owns part of the shared amount-selection policy.

scope.why: The changes are confined to schedule amount planning, API exposure, associated tests, and release notes.

maintainability.why: The shared arithmetic is straightforward, but duplicated dispatch and an optional untyped operator make consistent adoption harder to maintain.

bypasses_abstraction.where: packages/loot-core/src/server/budget/schedule-template.ts selects getRangeWorstCase or getApproxWorstCase locally instead of delegating amount selection to getScheduledAmount.

disguised_duplication.where: The operator-based nested ternary in schedule-template.ts reshapes the amount-selection logic implemented through type dispatch and an approximate-operator check in getScheduledAmount.

abstraction_drift.where: getScheduledAmount gains optional op?: string and an isapprox branch; schedule-template.ts independently dispatches to the lower-level helpers.
